rationale: Abraham's death and burial and Isaac's are told in the same sequence, checkable in the BSB. Abraham 'breathed his last and died, old and contented, and was gathered to his people', and 'His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him' (25:8-9). Isaac 'breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him' (35:29). By a script count over the BSB, 'breathed his last' and 'gathered to' stand together in only four verses of Genesis (25:8, 25:17, 35:29, 49:33), and 25:9 and 35:29 are the only two Genesis verses that name two sons together burying their father (in 50:14 Joseph alone is named). In each pair of sons the two had been separated earlier in the story (21:14; 27:41-28:5). Two named readers set the verses side by side. The Talmud (Bava Batra 16b) argues from the order of names: in 35:29 the elder, Esau, is named first, so the naming of Isaac before Ishmael in 25:9 is read as Ishmael yielding precedence. The Pulpit Commentary on 25:9 quotes Wordsworth: 'Funerals of parents are reconciliations of children (Genesis 35:29)'. Graded parallel at strong, following conn-gen20-wifesister-gen12, because the shared wording and sequence can be verified in both texts whatever a reader concludes from them; whether either burial shows a reconciliation is a reading the lesson reports in Positions, not something this row asserts.
